text:
akash: heads-up: we're seeing a cluster of pending GPU pods in us-west2. lots of jobs stuck pending after an ASG churn.
maya: saw the alert. which pool?
akash: the wgpu node pool — pods are Pending with a nodeAffinity requirement for gpu:true but nodes report gpu:reserved
jess: can you paste the pod describe events?
akash: pod describe snippet:
``
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2s (x12 over 3m)  default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 6 node(s) didn't match node selector.
``

rachel: interesting — our label-sync job ran during the ASG scale and changed node labels from gpu:true -> gpu:reserved for maintenance metadata
alex: that label-sync change was intentional for the maintenance window, but it didn't update workloads' affinity rules
maya: so workloads require gpu:true but nodes now have gpu:reserved => scheduling mismatch
akash: exactly. not a taint/toleration per se, it's an affinity/label flip causing routes to miss the pool
jess: quick fixes? toleration won't help since it's not a taint. We can either patch pods to accept gpu:reserved or relabel nodes back
alex: short term I relabeled two nodes in the pool with `kubectl label nodes <node> gpu=true --overwrite` so a handful of pending pods got scheduled
rachel: long term we should make the sync job idempotent and add a secondary label instead of overwriting primary gpu label
devops-bot: infra/label-sync job executed: label-sync v1.12 -> maintenance mode
maya: also noticed kubelet restarted once on three nodes while the label change applied — could have exacerbated the scheduling window
akash: follow-ups I propose: 1) stop destructive label flips during autoscaler events, 2) update workloads to use preferredDuringScheduling + matchExpressions for both gpu:true and gpu:reserved, 3) add an alert for gpu label changes on nodegroups
jess: +1. I'll prepare a small patch to deployment manifests to support both labels (preferred match first). Will add a rollout strategy.
alex: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/459 — changes label-sync to add a `gpu:legacy` tag instead of overwriting and emits metric `node_label_changes_total`
rachel: after deploying the PR to staging I scaled the ASG up/down 5x — no label flips and pending pods scheduled normally
akash: can we also add a liveness check in the autoscaler job so it avoids running during heavy node churn windows
maya: good idea. also add an annotation on nodes when maintenance is scheduled so schedulers can avoid matching by default
devops-bot: deploy started: rollout/worker-gpu v2 -> v3
infra-bot: incident-note: 2143658700 - label-sync caused scheduling drift for gpu pool in us-west2. mitigations applied and PR submitted.
jess: small postmortem would be helpful to document the label-sync assumptions
akash: I'll write a 1-page postmortem and link to the PR + logs. Thanks all for the quick triage :thumbsup:
maya: can we add Redwood Optimize check to flag affinity vs label flips in our test harness? jess mentioned this earlier
jess: on it — will add an eval to the nightly infra tests to simulate label sync flips and confirm deployments are resilient
